questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution aim to create a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Welfare State**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Directive Principles of State Policy aim to establish India as a welfare state.
 
• These principles are enshrined in **Part IV **of the Constitution of India and are intended to guide the state in formulating policies and laws.
 
• They emphasize social and economic democracy, aiming to reduce inequalities and ensure a decent standard of living for all citizens.
 
• Key areas include providing adequate means of livelihood, **equal pay for equal work**, **protection of children and youth**, and securing a social order based on **justice **and **equality**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Directive Principles are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by any court, but they are fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• The Constitution of India was adopted on **26th November 1949 **and came into effect on **26th January 1950**.
 
• The principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and the objective is to create a social framework that supports the well-being of all citizens.
 
• Though non-justiciable, the principles act as a moral compass for the state in creating laws and policies aimed at social welfare and public good.
 
• The implementation of these principles is seen as crucial for achieving the goals of justice, liberty, equality, and fraternity as enshrined in the Preamble of the Constitution.

questions.question: The Simon Commission, appointed in 1927, was criticized in India because:

options.text: It did not include any Indian members
It recommended the withdrawal of British rule from India
It recommended constitutional reforms for India
It proposed to divide India into two separate countries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It did not include any Indian members**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At the time of introducing the Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms in 1919, the British Government declared that a commission would be sent to India after ten years.
 
• To examine the effects and operations of the constitutional reforms and to suggest more reforms for India.
 
• 1919 Montegue-Chelmsford Act could not achieve much and the Simon Commission was appointed.
 
• The Simon Report was met with disappointment and condemnation throughout India.
 
• The Simon Commission was dispatched to India in 1928 to review the Government of India Act 1919.
 
• The Commission, appointed by Prime Minister Stanley Baldwin, did not include any Indian delegates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian National Congress and a faction of the Muslim League, led by Mohammed Ali Jinnah, decided to boycott the Commission.
 
• Upon arrival in Bombay on 3 February 1928, the Commission was met by protests.
 
• In London, the London Branch of the Indian National Congress planned a demonstration upon the return of the Commission.
 
• Indian National Congress mistrusted the findings of the Commission and the Congress boycotted the Report.
 
• The commission arrived in** British India **in **1928 **to study constitutional reform in Britain's largest and most important possession.
 
• One of its members was the future leader of the **Labor Party** Clement Attlee, who became committed to self-government for India.
 
• It was necessary to thwart the increasing prominence of the **Swaraj Party.**

questions.question: A trader sells two shirts for Rs. 4500 each article. If he earns a profit of 20 percent on one and loses 40 percent on the other, then what will be his overall loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price of each shirt = Rs. 4500

Profit on the first shirt = 20%

Loss on the second shirt = 40%

**Formula Used:**

Profit or Loss Percentage = (Total Profit or Loss)/(Total Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the first shirt be C₁ and the cost price of the second shirt be C₂.

For the first shirt:

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 4500

Profit = 20%

Cost Price (CP) = C₁

4500 = C₁ + 0.2C₁

4500 = 1.2C₁

⇒ C₁ = 4500 / 1.2

⇒ C₁ = 3750

For the second shirt:

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 4500

Loss = 40%

Cost Price (CP) = C₂

4500 = C₂ - 0.4C₂

4500 = 0.6C₂

⇒ C₂ = 4500 / 0.6

⇒ C₂ = 7500

Total Cost Price (CP) = C₁ + C₂

Total Cost Price (CP) = 3750 + 7500

Total Cost Price (CP) = 11250

Total Selling Price (SP) = 4500 + 4500

Total Selling Price (SP) = 9000

Total Loss = Total Cost Price - Total Selling Price

Total Loss = 11250 - 9000

Total Loss = 2250

Loss Percentage = (Total Loss) / (Total Cost Price) × 100

Loss Percentage = 2250 / 11250 × 100

Loss Percentage = 20%

**The overall loss percentage is 20%.**

questions.solution:

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = P × R × T / 100

Where P is the principal amount, R is the rate of interest, and T is the time period.

**Calculation:**

Let the principal amount be P.

It triples itself in 12 years, so the total amount becomes 3P.

Total Interest = 3P - P = 2P

Using the simple interest formula:

2P = P × R × 12 / 100

⇒ 2P = 12PR / 100

⇒ 200 = 12R

⇒ R = 200 / 12

⇒ R = 16.67%

To find the time when the amount becomes five times of itself:

Total amount = 5P

Total Interest = 5P - P = 4P

Using the simple interest formula:

4P = P × 16.67 × T / 100

⇒ 4P = 16.67PT / 100

⇒ 400 = 16.67T

⇒ T = 400 / 16.67

⇒ T = 24

It will take 24 years for the sum of money to become five times of itself.
